_deal: The live local-cargo pool, as every lettered recipe since 2026-10-12.
author: jessica, as Vance Okonkwo-Reyes
source: his 2026-10-12 18:15: "Do you want to try using a penname to write a delve?" and, on Vance, "yup go for it"
_note: THE FIRST DELVE WRITTEN UNDER A PEN NAME. The person is the sergeant herself: home-office
office/pennames/vance-okonkwo-reyes.json, named live the same evening. Her register: flat imperative, states
and never explains, answers a question with the action it implies, gives a count or a time where a warmer
voice gives a feeling. The one thing she will not count is what she carries; it is not said here at all.
Her heat checks do not apply (Overtime is adult, not explicit, his 10-12). Her voice floor does.
Beats are all known: talk (14a), two pickups (13a), a deliver that speaks (13a). No new template work,
unless one person who briefs at the talk and speaks again at the deliver needs it.
Voiced lines: no names, no places, no flags. 'Navy' is a role; she never says which navy.
MODELS: the relay dish (approved, his rig) stands in for the comms mast until Kim's kitbash has a mesh path;
the power cell is vanilla Power_Cell_Static_PackinOnly (Kim's carries pass, C4).

place._theme: A quiet worked site with a relay on it. She is placed by the talk beat: NonHostile mostly has nobody.

prose.name: Repairs: Relay Power on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A relay post at the <Place> wants a contractor to carry two power cells. The posting is short and signed with a rank.

beats.objective: Report to the sergeant at the <Place>
beats.journal: The sergeant at the <Place> keeps the relay running alone. Two power cells are waiting at the drop. She wants them in the relay, left bay first.

person.name: Sergeant Okafor
person._outfit: WANTED: a vanilla Navy or UC service outfit; Eliza or Kim picks the EditorID. Never guessed here.
person._elevenlabs: Petra's voice reused as a placeholder. She wants flat and clipped, not chill. His ear.

beats.greeting: You're the contractor. Eleven minutes late. Cells are at the drop. Two. Go.

exchanges.reply: Two. Don't drop them. Left bay first, then right. I'll have the panel open.

exchanges.prompt: Why can't you fetch them yourself?
exchanges.reply: Relay can't be left. Standing order. Not mine. I follow it.
Relay needs one. Rations for one. Cells for one. Next drop in nine days.

exchanges.prompt: Buy you a drink when you're off?
exchanges.reply: Off in nine days. Ask me then. Cells first.

beats._talk: PROPOSED fields, as 14a. Exchange 0 ends the conversation and sets the first pickup's stage. Exchange 3 is the flirt his 10-12 ceiling allows, answered in register: with the action it implies.

message.title: Relay Power Cell
message.text: A power cell, signed for in advance. The signature is a rank and a surname. Someone has written LEFT on the casing.

message.title: Relay Power Cell
message.text: The second cell. RIGHT, in the same hand. The letters are exactly the same height.

beats.objective: Fit the power cells to the relay
beats.journal: A sergeant keeping a relay post alone at the <Place> needed two power cells carried. I carried them. She said next, and meant it.
beats.name: Relay
beats.say: Left bay. Good. Right bay. Good. Relay's up. Payment's sent. Next.

broadcast: Relay post needs a contractor. Two cells to carry. Paid on completion. Out.
_speech: Her voice on the radio, in person and at the relay. No names, no places, no flags.
